newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. says turned back three Iraqi oil contracts.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says turned back three Iraqi oil contracts.

text.p: Three additional oil contracts submitted by Iraq for United Nations approval were turned back for resubmission on technical grounds Wednesday, a U.N. spokesman said.

"Four contracts have been requested for resubmission since the oil deal started," said the spokesman, noting that total included one contract from Tuesday, the first day of the U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food deal.

Only one contract has been approved by the U.N.-appointed oil overseers since the plan's start. The Turkish state oil company TUPRAS successfully completed a deal to lift 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi crude on Tuesday.

U.N. sources have stated that the one contract needing resubmission from Tuesday was between Iraq and Elf Aquitaine. That contract was submitted incorrectly, and was denied approval on procedural grounds, the U.N. has said.
No details were available on why the three additional oil contracts were denied immediate approval Wednesday.
"It must also have been on procedural, technical grounds," said the spokesman.
Diplomats working closely on the Iraqi deal said they doubted the contracts were turned back for any substantive reason.
Since the deal's start at 0501 GMT Tuesday, there have been a total of five contracts posted to the overseers, one being approved and four turned back.
Oil companies were seeking contracts to take part in the $2 billion oil-for-food plan, which allows Iraqi oil sales for the first time since Baghdad invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
Nearly two-thirds of the oil revenues gathered over the six-month, renewable period for the deal were earmarked for purchases of food and aid for needy Iraqi civilians.
